title: The message behind Christopher Nolan’s most important change to “The Odyssey”
gist: Yglesias argues the biggest and least-discussed change Christopher Nolan made to 'The Odyssey' is inserting the Sea Peoples and the Bronze Age Collapse, an anachronistic framing drawn from Eric Cline's '1177 B.C.' that subverts Homer by implying the Trojan War seeded Mycenaean Greece's own destruction. He reads the film's message as a claim that the West risks collapse from abandoning its own values rather than from external enemies. (Post is a paid-subscriber piece; the available text cuts off partway through the 'two ancient Greeces' section.)
